Alexander, at {{height|ft=6|in=8}} played both [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] positions,[http://www.nba.com/bucks/features/alexander_chat_080926.html Chat with Joe Alexander] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150122111516/http://www.nba.com/bucks/features/alexander_chat_080926.html |date=January 22, 2015 }}, NBA.com, September 26, 2008 was selected for the 2007 All-[[Big East Conference|Big East]] squad during his [[college basketball|collegiate career]] with [[West Virginia Mountaineers|West Virginia]] and was an [[All-American]] Honorable Mention. He was selected eighth overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], and became the first Taiwanese-born NBA player.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_joe_alexander_2010_09_20.html |title=HORNETS: Hornets Sign Joe Alexander |publisher=NBA |access-date=January 6, 2012}} ==Early life and education== Born in [[Kaohsiung]], Taiwan, Alexander moved to [[Silver Spring, Maryland]], when he was two. When he was eight, his family relocated to China when his father got a job working for [[Nestlé]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/MB_081015.html |title=Alexander returns to birthplace of dreams |publisher=NBA |date=October 15, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} His maternal grandfather was Jewish, which made him eligible for [[Israeli citizenship]] while playing for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/sports/crushed-maccabi-looks-ahead-to-next-year-398863|title=Crushed Maccabi looks ahead to next year|website=The Jerusalem Post |date=April 22, 2015 }} Alexander lived in Hong Kong for six months and then in mainland China for six years, becoming conversant in [[Mandarin Chinese|Mandarin]]. While Alexander lived in Hong Kong, he attended the [[Hong Kong International School]] in [[Tai Tam]]. Alexander and his family lived in a separated ex-pat community with other Americans in Beijing.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/draft2008/alexander_20080625.html |title=The Journey Less Traveled |publisher=NBA |date=June 25, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} There he attended the [[International School of Beijing]] from 1996 to 2002, where he first became acquainted with basketball.{{citation|url=http://www.denizenmag.com/2009/06/im-a-tck-and-i-play-for-the-nba/|periodical=Denizen Magazine|date=June 2009|last=Dube|first=Wazha|title=I'm a TCK… and I play for the NBA |access-date=September 17, 2011}} His brothers, John and Jeremy, became the first foreigners to win the Beijing High School basketball MVP award and did so in successive seasons. In 2010, the ISB Dragons basketball team officially retired Alexander's jersey in an elaborate ceremony in the school gym, a ceremony where Alexander himself was present. Alexander then returned to the U.S. to live in [[Mount Airy, Maryland]], where he spent his junior and senior seasons playing for [[Linganore High School]]. While he only played a minor role coming off the bench his junior year, his senior season he boasted averages of 14.8 points, 7.0 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game, which earned him first-team Monocacy Valley Athlete League Chesapeake conference honors. Alexander was named team captain his senior year and selected to the Frederick County all-star first team. He was named Mt. Airy Gazette player of the year, 2004 Frederick Gazette player of the year, earned first-team honors from the Frederick Gazette and Frederick News Post, and was on ''[[The Washington Post]]''{{'}}s honorable mention all-Met team. Alexander also set school records for blocks in a season (90) and season field-goal percentage (58.0). After high school, Alexander gained only limited attention from [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] schools (including [[Washington College]], where his brothers were playing) and some [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] programs despite having a good senior season. At that point, Alexander was {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|abbr=on}} and only {{convert|170|lb|abbr=on}}; a [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] athletic scholarship was out of the question. Determined to make his dream a reality, he opted to attend [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in Chatham, Virginia. Playing behind Pitt star [[Sam Young (basketball)|Sam Young]] and Villanova's [[Shane Clark (basketball)|Shane Clark]], Alexander saw limited playing time while at Hargrave. ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Alexander enrolled at [[West Virginia University]] in 2005 after attending [[Hargrave Military Academy]] for the 2004–2005 season. As a freshman, he played in 10 games, while starters [[Kevin Pittsnogle]] and [[Mike Gansey]] led the starting senior class. On November 13, 2005, Alexander scored his first collegiate basket against [[Wofford College|Wofford]].{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=27301&year=2006 |title=Joe Alexander Game Log: 2005–2006 Season |publisher=ESPN |date=January 2, 2011 |access-date=January 6, 2012}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} His best game his freshman year was against [[Washington & Jefferson Presidents|Washington & Jefferson College]] where he scored five points and blocked five shots on December 3.{{cite web|author=WVU Coliseum, Morgantown, WV |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=253370277 |title=Wash & Jefferson 33, West Virginia 83 |publisher=ESPN |date=December 3, 2005 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} === Sophomore season === Alexander finally started in the 2006–2007 season. Against [[DePaul University|DePaul]] on January 28, 2007, Alexander posted a career-high 23 points. With 90 seconds left in the game, West Virginia led 61–48 after Alexander's shot-clock-beating 3-pointer and a three-point play.{{cite web|author=WVU Coliseum, Morgantown, WV |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270280277 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306234807/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270280277 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |title=DePaul vs. West Virginia – Recap – January 28, 2007 |publisher=ESPN |date=January 28, 2007 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} But from what looked to be a good season, Alexander's season declined in the second half. After an 11-point performance versus [[Providence College|Providence]] on February 2,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270512507 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306234858/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=270512507 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |title=Mountaineers miss 32 3s in loss to unranked Providence |publisher=ESPN |date=February 20, 2007 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} Alexander went without scoring over double-digits for the rest of the regular season{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/gamelog?playerId=27301&year=2007 |title=Joe Alexander Game Log: 2006–2007 Season |publisher=ESPN |date=January 2, 2011 |access-date=January 6, 2012}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} and the [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]]. Afterwards, West Virginia alumnus [[Bob Huggins]] left [[Kansas State]] for the head coaching job at WVU. Huggins emphasizes strength training and as a result Alexander went from 210 pounds to 230 pounds and has often remarked that the training allowed him to avoid fatigue and weight loss.{{cite web |url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?cat=exclusives&sport=&startrow=1 |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |access-date=January 6, 2012 |archive-date=June 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120607110006/http://msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?cat=exclusives&sport=&startrow=1 |url-status=dead }} In the season-opening exhibition game against [[Mountain State University|Mountain State]], Alexander scored 19 points, grabbed 6 rebounds, totaled 5 blocks, and had one steal in the 88–65 win. Alexander contributed with a career-high 34 points,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280730041 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306234837/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280730041 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 6, 2019 |title=Alexander's 34 points lift West Virginia past Connecticut |publisher=ESPN |date=March 13, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} the most ever by a Mountaineer in a Big East championship. He also added 7 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=280730041 |title=West Virginia 78, (17) Connecticut 72 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 13, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} The game marked his third 30-point game of the season. However, as the Mountaineers lost in the semifinal matchup against the No. 8 [[Georgetown Hoyas]], Alexander finished the Big East tournament with 12 points on 5-of-16 shooting,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280740046 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170319112134/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=280740046 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 19, 2017 |title=Hoyas reach another Big East final behind Hibbert's 25 points, 13 boards |publisher=ESPN |date=March 14, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} and 5 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=280740046 |title=West Virginia 55, (8) Georgetown 72 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 14, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} The Mountaineers' run to the semifinal round of the Big East Tourney propelled the team to a #7 seed in the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]], with a first-round matchup against the #10 seed [[Arizona Wildcats]]. [[ESPN]], in their West region breakdown, named Alexander the best player in the region next to [[UCLA]]'s [[Kevin Love]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/ncaatourney08/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=3297732 |title="Bulldogs are the Cinderella stories of the West, but chalk may reign" – ESPN |publisher=ESPN |date=March 17, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} In the first-round victory over Arizona, Alexander scored 14 points and grabbed 8 rebounds.{{cite web|author=Verizon Center, Washington, DC |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=284000042 |title=(10) Arizona 65, (7) West Virginia 75 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 20, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} In the second-round victory over the #2-seed [[Duke Blue Devils]], he scored 22 points and grabbed 11 rebounds as the Mountaineers won 73–67.{{cite web|author=Verizon Center, Washington, DC |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000044 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190210100051/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000044 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 10, 2019 |title=West Virginia's defense, rebounding send Duke to another early NCAA exit |publisher=ESPN |date=March 22, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} In the Sweet 16 75–79 overtime loss to No. 3 [[Xavier University|Xavier]] on March 27, Alexander scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds for his second double-double of the tournament.{{cite web|author=US Airways Center, Phoenix, AZ |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000045 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170323140546/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000045 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 23, 2017 |title=Raymond saves Xavier with two 3-pointers in last 1:18 of overtime |publisher=ESPN |date=March 27, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} Alexander finished his junior season leading the team with 16.9 points per game and 6.4 rebounds per game. Alexander was second on the team with 1.5 blocks per game and third with 2.4 assists per game and 31.6 minutes played per game. He finished the NCAA Tournament by averaging 18 points and 9.6 rebounds per game. ==Professional career== ===Milwaukee Bucks (2008–2010)=== On April 9, 2008, Alexander declared himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]], and later signed with an agent, forfeiting his remaining college eligibility. Alexander was described as the best athlete on paper at the draft overall, by having the second-most number of 185-pound bench reps (24), the second-highest max touch (12' ½") and the second-fastest three-quarter sprint time (2.99 seconds). He was drafted 8th overall in the [[2008 NBA draft|NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in June,{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/alexander_080626.html |title=BUCKS: Bucks select Alexander in the 2008 NBA Draft |publisher=NBA |date=June 26, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} and was signed by the team on July 8.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/alexander_signs_080708.html |title=Bucks Sign First round Pick Joe Alexander |publisher=NBA |date=July 8, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} In the 2008 [[NBA Summer League]], Alexander averaged 9.2 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game while starting all five games. In a December 7, 2008 Bucks loss to the, Alexander led the team in scoring with 15 points.{{cite web|author=STAPLES Center, Los Angeles, CA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281207013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919024937/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281207013 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 19, 2018 |title=Lakers roll over Bucks to equal franchise-best 17–2 start |publisher=ESPN |date=December 7, 2008 |access-date=January 6, 2012}} Following the All-Star break, Alexander saw a streak of four consecutive games where he did not play. However, he rebounded in a loss to the [[Miami Heat]] by totaling 13 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists in 20 minutes of playing time. He averaged 5.8 points for the month of January, the most of his rookie season in a month. In a March 30, 2009 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]], Alexander scored a career-high 16 points.{{cite web |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NBA&id=1486&line=113862&spln=1 |title=Joe Alexander scores a career-high 16 points |publisher=Rotoworld.com |access-date=January 6, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615191523/http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NBA&id=1486&line=113862&spln=1 |archive-date=June 15, 2011 }} Alexander finished the season averaging 4.7 points in his 12.1 minutes per game. In the offseason prior to the 2009–2010 season, starting forward [[Richard Jefferson]] was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], potentially freeing up playing time for Alexander. On October 30, 2009, the Bucks declined Alexander's rookie contract option that would have added a third season to his rookie contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/alexander_091102.html |title=Bucks elect not to exercise option on Joe Alexander |work=Milwaukee Bucks |publisher=NBA |access-date=January 6, 2012}} After missing time because of a hamstring injury, Alexander was assigned to the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]'s [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] on January 20, 2010.{{cite web |author=Steve Warden |work=The Journal Gazette |url=http://www.journalgazette.net/article/20100120/SPORTS0603/100129957/1008/SPORTS |title=Bucks assign Alexander to Mad Ants |date=January 20, 2010 |access-date=January 6, ===Texas Legends (2010–2011)=== On November 26, Alexander was signed by the NBA D-League's [[Texas Legends]]. He had a successful 2010–11 season with the Legends averaging 20.2 points and 8.9 rebounds per game and was awarded a spot at the D-League's 2011 All-Star game. He was in an [[Atlanta Hawks]] minicamp before the [[2011 NBA lockout]] occurred. In June 2011, Alexander was listed as one of the NBA's "Biggest Draft Busts" by the ''[[New York Daily News]]'', due to his struggles to transition from college to the NBA.{{cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nba-draft-biggest-draft-busts-gallery-1.60176 |title=NBA Draft: Biggest Draft Busts Ever |work=NY Daily News |access-date=January 6, 2012}} ===Krasnye Krylia (2011)=== In July 2011, Alexander signed with [[BC Krasnye Krylia|BC Krasnye Krylya Samara]] of Russia.{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/russia/29862/krasnye_krylya_samara_lands_joe_alexander_and_jarvis_hayes.html |title=Krasnye Krylya Samara lands Joe Alexander and Jarvis Hayes |work=Sportando.net |date=July 25, 2011|access-date=November 7, 2013}} He left in December 2011, after an X-ray revealed Alexander had a [[stress fracture]] in his left [[tibia]]. After a sabbatical year hoping the injury would heal itself, Alexander opted to fix his tibia through surgery in 2012.[http://www.santacruzsentinel.com/santacruz/ci_25403201/d-league-basketball-santa-cruz-warriors-forward-joe D-League Basketball: Santa Cruz Warriors forward Joe Alexander is back on the rebound], Santa Cruz Sentinel ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2013–2014)=== On September 27, 2013, Alexander signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14351|title=Warriors sign Ognjen Kuzmic; add Joe Alexander to training camp – NBA Blog|date=September 27, 2013 }} On October 25, 2013, Alexander was waived by the Warriors.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-joe-alexander-seth-curry-and-dewayne-dedmon|title=Warriors Waive Joe Alexander, Seth Curry and Dewayne Dedmon|website=Golden State Warriors}} The reason was a [[magnetic resonance imaging]] showed his leg was not fully recovered yet. Instead Alexander was signed by team's D-League affiliate, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]], where treatment was administered to both his leg and overall muscle performance. A recovered Alexander played 13 games for Santa Cruz in the 2013–14 regular season. In the playoffs, Alexander appeared in 4 games through the Warriors' D-League runners-up campaign.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/teams/SAN/2014.html|title=2013-14 Santa
